design: Root controller remains outside a dedicated nondelegated cgroup-v2 scope. Actor enters before native execution. Root freezes only the retirement barrier, validates exact registered control processes, retains correlated evidence and always thaws. Preserve native cleanup; equivalent_native_settled is separate.

original_conditions.basis: Original protocol lines70-81 requires equal resources and bounded work including helpers; lines83-91 preserves incomplete outcomes and unknown usage. It does not prescribe the OpenClaw cleanup field. Actual termination may be independently proved without overwriting uncertain or claiming task success.
original_conditions.preserve: Same native user/profile/route/tools/model roles/network/clock and per-case envelope; no CPU/memory/pids/network limit or inherited resource-envelope change. Bookkeeping/freezer overhead remains within the existing monotonic deadline.
original_conditions.privileges: Dormant parent line91 already drops groups and capability sets. NoNewPrivs must not remove an originally admitted service or silently replace native policy; it supplies exec privilege containment, not new actor authority.

minimum_required_facts.requirement: Root establishes a real domain cgroup and immutable identity before any actor/native fork or exec. Verify actor membership at a launch barrier, with PID/starttime, boot/PID namespace and scope filesystem identity. Migrating a parent after children exist is insufficient.

Delegate=no; root-only directory and migration controls, including common ancestors. Observe UID/groups/capability sets/NoNewPrivs and no actor-writable migration FD. Any admitted external execution broker must also be scoped/accounted or equivalence is refused. NoNewPrivs alone does not prove this.

Root records exact control PID+starttime identities before workload; no names, wildcard ancestry or actor-provided allowlist. SO_PEERCRED binds peer identity and cgroup; root independently reads kernel membership. Peer credentials do not authenticate actor-supplied census contents.

After matching pre-close readback and physical exit, admissions remain closed. Root outside the scope freezes it, waits for frozen=1, checks every live member/descendant against the fixed control identities, saves the receipt and thaws in finally within the same deadline. Unexpected members or missing/raced evidence refuse. A live unfrozen cgroup.procs snapshot minus allowlist is insufficient.

Retain existing complete current-sample usage, zero pending SDK/tools, actual native client readbacks/background-terminal checks and queue flushes. Observe the exact pinned factory result for this client/turn. Missing observation or active authority refuses equivalence absent separate release proof. Factory absence covers only that branch, not all possible in-process delegated work; active or unobserved delegated work must also refuse.

Receipt binds scope generation, client/exit, admitted thread+turn hashes, clock generation, private readback hash, census and authority/pending facts. Refuse missing/stale/replayed/mismatched evidence. Recheck owner stop/deadline after retention and before continuation. Do not extend caps or reset counters.

Keep native cleanup=uncertain and native_closed=false exactly as returned. equivalent_native_settled requires the whole conjunction above, never exit alone or post-test emptiness. Errors/timeouts and original quality/scorer remain separate.

kernel_references.facts: Forked children inherit membership; moving a parent does not move existing descendants. Migration needs destination/common-ancestor write access. cgroup.procs is not an atomic ordered process snapshot. Freezing reports completion via cgroup.events; populated is recursive. These support scope accounting without new resource limits.
The inherited flag blocks exec-based setuid/file-capability gains, not existing privileges or non-exec privilege transfer.
